newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly higher on soy gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly higher on soy gains.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mostly firmer on Friday, following strength in soybeans tied to news analysts were expecting a cut in USDA's ending stocks figure, traders said.

Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel told Reuters he projected ending stocks at 125 million bushels although he added that USDA would probably put the number closer to 140 million. He attributed the cut primarily to heavy crush rates.
USDA on Wednesday will release its Supply/Demand Report. Last month USDA cut its soybean ending stocks estimate to 155 million bushels from 180 million a month earlier.
Traders noted there was little input from world markets as several major holidays converged, slowing world trade and limiting demand for soy products.

Chinese usage was expected to slow to a trickle as the country observed the Lunar New Year. Meanwhile, Muslim countries were observing Eid al-Fitr, which marks the end of Ramadan. Indian trade was also shut down on Friday in observance of a Hindu religious holiday.
Soymeal closed $2.80 per ton higher to $0.50 lower with March up $2.80 at $235.30. Soyoil ended up 0.10 cent per lb to down 0.01 with March up 0.07 at 23.93.

Weather in South America continued to lend a bearish undertone. Conditions were stable in Brazil's key soybean growing regions, with growers expecting some rain over the weekend, Brazilian sources said.
On the day, ADM sold 300 lots May soyoil, Produce Grain sold 100 March and bought 200 March and 100 May, traders said.

In soymeal, Griffin Trading sold 400 lots March and Prudential Securities sold 200 March and 150 May. Refco Inc and Rosenthal Collins each sold 200 March. E.D. and F. Man International bought 250 March.
Soyoil volume was estimated by CBOT at 11,000 lots, against Thursday's actual volume of 11,709 lots. Soymeal volume was pegged at 18,000 lots, compared with Thursday's 23,264 lots.
